title: Marketing strategy
subtitle: A clear 90-day plan before you write a single line
intro: Without a strategy, every post and every campaign heads in a different direction. In this chapter, you use Claude like a demanding business partner: it helps you take an honest look at where you stand, set a measurable goal, pick three priorities and turn it all into a 90-day plan you follow week by week.

steps.d: Gather what works, what's stuck and your current numbers so you start from your real situation, not an ideal one.
Pick a single measurable 90-day goal tied to your revenue, and write it in one sentence.
Keep three projects at most that directly serve the goal, and write down what you're stopping to make room.
Break the plan into weekly actions and do a quick review every Friday to adjust what isn't working.

prompts.title: The quick diagnosis
prompts.use: Before planning, to know exactly where you're starting from.
prompts.prompt: You are a marketing director who works with small businesses. Before suggesting anything, ask me 8 questions, one at a time, to understand my business: [YOUR BUSINESS], my current clients, my channels, my monthly budget of [BUDGET] and the time I have available. Wait for my answer before each new question. At the end, summarize my situation in a 3-column table: What works, What's stuck, What's missing. Finish with the 2 problems to tackle first, with one sentence of reasoning for each.

prompts.title: From wish to goal
prompts.use: When your goal is vague, like “get more clients.”
prompts.prompt: Act as a straight-talking business coach. My current goal is: [YOUR VAGUE GOAL]. My starting point: [CURRENT NUMBERS: REVENUE, NUMBER OF CLIENTS, LEADS PER MONTH]. Suggest 3 versions of this goal, each one measurable, with a 90-day deadline and realistic given my starting point. For each version, give: the metric to track, the target value, what it requires from me each week and the main risk. Present everything in a table, then recommend one version and explain your choice in 3 sentences.

prompts.title: The 12-week plan
prompts.use: Once your goal is set, to get a week-by-week plan.
prompts.prompt: You are the marketing lead in a small team of [TEAM SIZE] people. 90-day goal: [GOAL]. Chosen priorities: [PRIORITY 1], [PRIORITY 2], [PRIORITY 3]. Time available: [HOURS PER WEEK]. Build a 12-week plan in a table with these columns: Week, Priority, Concrete action, Deliverable, Estimated time, Metric. Group the weeks into 3 phases of 30 days and give each phase a name. Never go over the available time, and flag any week that is overloaded.

prompts.title: The plan stress test
prompts.use: Before you start, to spot the weak points in your plan.
prompts.prompt: Here is my 90-day marketing plan: [PASTE YOUR PLAN]. Play the role of a skeptical investor who has seen many plans fail. List the 5 most serious weaknesses, from most to least risky. For each one, give: why it's a problem, the signal that will show it's going off track, and a concrete fix. Be blunt, no compliments. End with the one action to cut from the plan if I run short on time, and explain why.

workflow.title: Workflow: your 90-day plan in a Claude Project
steps: Create a “Marketing 2026” Project and add your business overview, offers and recent numbers as files.
Run “The quick diagnosis” and answer the questions without dressing up your situation.
Turn your wish into a goal with the second prompt, then pick three priorities at most.
Ask for the 12-week plan in an Artifact so you can review, edit and copy it easily.
Add the final plan to the Project files so every new conversation starts from it.

checklist: My goal fits in one sentence, with a number and a date.
I track this goal with one main metric.
I have three priorities at most, not one more.
I wrote down what I'm stopping for these 90 days.
Every week of the plan has a concrete action and deliverable.
The plan fits the time I actually have.
mistake: Common mistake: asking straight away for “a marketing plan.” With no context, Claude gives you a generic plan that works for everyone, so it's useful to no one.
tip: Dr. Firas's tip: every Friday, paste your weekly results into the Project and ask Claude what to keep, cut or adjust the following week.
